_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-commit-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_ledger_commit_cites_no_rows.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when a violation has an EMPTY REPAIR SPACE: the commit is pushed and cannot be amended, a revert cannot clear a gate that reads subjects across the marker range, and re-anchoring the marker past the violation would make the marker's own definition false and silently convert a live violation into an excused one. Key every entry by the FULL 40-character sha copied from live git output — a short sha or a tag matches nothing while looking like it should. The entry must PROVE the empty repair space and state the reason. It is printed as an 'excused:' line on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. A malformed entry, or one that matches no violation, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. A second entry of the same shape is a process defect, not an exemption: one is a debt, two mean the mechanism — running tools/audit.py before a commit that touches the ledger — is not biting. THIS file also carries the clause's ANCHOR, and the shipped default is NOT it: the gate's default marker is the first commit touching the ledger whose subject obeys the clause IN THE TEMPLATE'S OWN HISTORY, and a factory bootstrapped from the template does not carry that history — so the gate SKIPs there with its reason rather than passing vacuously. Declare `marker` as the first commit touching evidence/ledger.jsonl in YOUR history whose subject obeys the clause, and the gate begins judging your range. A marker that does not RESOLVE is a gate FAILURE, never a skip: a declared parameter that cannot be honoured is a defect, not an absence. This is the same shape as tests/ledger_boundary.py's declared boundary (issue #78, P35) — the gate's LOGIC is universal, its PARAMETERS are factory data, because this file is byte-paired into TEMPLATE/ and editing a sha in it is either a fork or a pair-gate RED.
